claims.text: Applying an Al2O3 coating to a refractory high-entropy alloy can improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
The intervention is applicable to refractory high-entropy alloys in either an as-cast or as-sintered state.
The Al2O3 coating should provide protection above 500°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere.
A stable protective oxide film forms via tribo-oxidation.
The Al2O3 coating acts as a barrier to oxygen penetration into the alloy.
Preventing oxygen penetration reduces degradation of the alloy.
The coated alloy will exhibit improved oxidation resistance and reduced degradation relative to an untreated alloy.
The proposed protection should operate from 500°C to 900°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere.
At 800°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere, oxidation weight gain and oxide-layer microstructure can distinguish coated from uncoated samples.
Failure of the coated sample to show a significant oxidation-resistance improvement over the uncoated sample would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify temperatures above 500°C, whereas the boundary includes 500°C.
The mediator invokes tribo-oxidation, which requires tribological contact or sliding, but the proposed oxidation experiment specifies no wear or rubbing condition.

The intervention supplies an already formed Al2O3 layer, while the mediator describes formation of a protective oxide film by tribo-oxidation without explaining what additional film forms or why tribological oxidation is required.
